Resolves #20894

An outside contributor with five merged PRs across public `neomjs` repositories may hold two open curated issues in Engine. The workflow searches once for the contributor’s standing and checks active assignments directly in this repository. If standing is unavailable it still answers using one slot. The fifth merge comment announces the new allowance.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Verification |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | Outside-CI: `claimLimit` uses the existing Returning Contributor rung. The spec checks zero, four, five and 250 merges. |
| AC-2 | Outside-CI: The workflow replay assigns a second claim at five merges and refuses a third. The default and lower standing refuse a second. Serialized bursts read fresh assignments even when search lags. |
| AC-3 | Outside-CI: The refusal names the issues that use the slots and explains the five-merge threshold to a contributor with one slot. |
| AC-4 | Outside-CI: `claimResponse.mjs` remains import-free. The legacy `decideReply(options)` string/null contract, single slot and three-day claim window remain in place. |
| AC-5 | Outside-CI: The workflow still responds with one slot after a refused or incomplete count or an unloadable standing module. Missing suggested alternatives cannot block the answer. |
| AC-6 | Outside-CI: The two-claim sentence appears on the fifth merge only. Tests cover the preceding, following and later milestone comments. |

## Deltas from ticket

The workflow accepts only the current one- or two-slot policy. Unsupported limits fall back to one. A third slot would require a policy change in both the decision and the workflow.

The operator also requested retries after a refusal. When a fresh request is still blocked, the Engine workflow updates its existing bot-authored refusal with the claim it evaluated. It posts one new confirmation only when it can grant the claim; replaying a covered event has no effect. The reply-only consumers keep their existing one-reply contract. A new explicit claim checks live ownership and capacity; an old event replay or a thank-you cannot acquire the issue. Previously posted refusals are recognized. A refused claim no longer holds the queue against another contributor. The regression includes two people commenting before the first workflow run finishes.

`CONTRIBUTING.md` now describes the limits, retry, a short handoff comment after pushing a requested fix, and maintainer responsibility for routine merge-train integration. No new notification producer is added.

## Test Evidence

Evidence: L3 local workflow replay at `c0e6d64109`. All 1,238 tests in the official build-scripts unit selection passed with dependencies installed from the lockfile. The workflow fixture executes the actual GitHub script with controlled API replies.

## Post-Merge Validation

On a subsequent genuine claim and qualifying fifth merge, observe the published reply and assignment. The shared maintainer pickup order is covered separately in [Skills #391](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/pull/391).

Authored by Emmy (Codex). Origin Session ID: d2972912-1050-4e40-8f00-ca193b527781.

**Open for the independent read** (the retry is outside my draft)

1. **How many replies can one account draw?** Until now the marker allowed one reply per claimant per issue. Now `reply && (!refusedClaim(reply, self) || !follows(comment, reply))` reopens the decision for every claim-shaped comment after a refusal. An account at capacity can therefore draw one bot reply per comment on any curated issue. Is that bounded anywhere?
2. **Who loses the line.** `earlierClaim` drops an earlier claimant whose claim a bot refusal covers. An earlier claimant who was refused for capacity, frees a slot and does not comment again loses the issue to the next claimant. The guide says to comment `/claim` again, so this looks intended; the arm "a queued claimant can proceed when the first claim was refused while the workflow was running" is the one to read against it.
3. **Old replies read by their opening words.** `refusedClaim()` takes a reply that opens with "you're already assigned to" or "this one is taken:" as a refusal. Worth one look that no assigning reply can open that way.
4. **The guide's new promise.** "We'll handle mechanical integration where we have permission" is a commitment to outside authors. It should match what the outside-PR pickup rule lets a maintainer do.

Checked and fine: `/claim` at the start of a line is a claim pattern, so the guide's instruction is one the responder hears.
